The present invention relates to methods and compositions for treating diseases, disorders, or pathological conditions associated with activating mutations in the GNAQ gene, particularly mutations resulting in substitution of arginine at position 183 with glutamine (R183Q) or glutamine at position 209 with leucine (Q209L). Such mutations are implicated in abnormal cellular proliferation, increased cell survival, and aberrant vascular development, including vascular malformations and other disorders characterized by cellular overgrowth.

The invention is based, at least in part, on the finding that puromycin, as well as structurally or functionally related puromycin analogs, can selectively inhibit proliferation and/or reduce survival of cells harboring disease-associated GNAQ mutations. Accordingly, in one aspect, the invention provides a method of treating a subject having, suspected of having, or at risk of developing a GNAQ mutation-associated disease or condition. The method comprises administering to the subject an effective amount of puromycin or a puromycin analog, or a pharmaceutical composition comprising the same, in an amount sufficient to reduce the growth, viability, survival, or pathological activity of cells comprising a GNAQ R183Q or GNAQ Q209L mutation.

In certain embodiments, the disease or condition is a vascular anomaly, vascular malformation, capillary malformation, venous malformation, lymphatic malformation, arteriovenous malformation, or another disorder involving abnormal vascular endothelial cell growth or function. In other embodiments, the condition includes cellular overgrowth, tissue enlargement, tumor-like lesions, or other proliferative abnormalities associated with a GNAQ activating mutation. The affected cells may include endothelial cells, vascular-associated cells, stromal cells, or other cell populations in which mutant GNAQ signaling contributes to disease pathogenesis.

The puromycin or puromycin analog may be administered locally, regionally, or systemically, depending on the location and severity of the disease. In some embodiments, the compound is delivered directly to a lesion, vascular malformation, or affected tissue. In other embodiments, it is formulated for topical, injectable, implantable, or controlled-release administration. The treatment may be used alone or in combination with one or more additional therapeutic agents, including agents that inhibit signaling pathways activated downstream of mutant GNAQ, anti-proliferative agents, anti-angiogenic agents, anti-inflammatory agents, or agents used in the management of vascular anomalies.

The invention further provides methods for reducing the viability or proliferation of a cell harboring a GNAQ R183Q or Q209L mutation. Such methods comprise contacting the cell with puromycin or a puromycin analog under conditions sufficient to inhibit growth, induce cell death, reduce metabolic activity, or otherwise suppress survival of the mutant cell. The method may be performed in vitro, ex vivo, or in vivo. In particular embodiments, mutant GNAQ cells are more sensitive to puromycin or a puromycin analog than corresponding wild-type cells, thereby permitting selective targeting of diseased or abnormal cells while reducing effects on non-mutant tissue.

In another aspect, the invention provides a screening method for identifying agents that modulate diseases or cellular phenotypes associated with mutant GNAQ. The method comprises providing cells comprising a GNAQ R183Q or GNAQ Q209L mutation, exposing the cells to puromycin and a candidate agent, and measuring a change in cell viability, proliferation, survival, metabolic activity, apoptosis, or another detectable cellular response. A candidate agent is identified as a modulator of a GNAQ mutation-associated disease or condition when it alters the response of the mutant cells to puromycin, for example by increasing or decreasing puromycin-induced reduction in viability, modifying cell proliferation, or otherwise affecting survival of the mutant cells.

In some embodiments, the screening method compares the effect of the candidate agent in mutant GNAQ cells with its effect in control cells, such as wild-type GNAQ cells or cells lacking the relevant mutation. Such comparison may identify compounds that selectively enhance killing of mutant cells, protect non-mutant cells, or reveal pathways involved in puromycin sensitivity. The screening method may be used to identify therapeutic agents, combination therapies, biomarkers of response, or molecular pathways relevant to treatment of GNAQ mutation-associated vascular malformations and related diseases.

The invention therefore provides both therapeutic and discovery applications. Therapeutically, puromycin or puromycin analogs may be used to suppress abnormal growth or survival of cells carrying GNAQ R183Q or Q209L mutations. Experimentally, the response of mutant GNAQ cells to puromycin can serve as a platform for identifying additional compounds that modulate disease-associated cellular phenotypes. Together, these approaches support the development of targeted treatments for vascular malformations and other disorders driven by activating mutations in GNAQ.

## GNAQ: An Overview

**GNAQ** is a gene that provides instructions for making a protein called **guanine nucleotide-binding protein subunit alpha-q**. This protein is part of a family of signaling proteins known as **G proteins**, which help transmit signals from the outside of a cell to the inside. These signals influence many important cellular processes, including growth, movement, communication, and survival.

The GNAQ protein is activated by certain cell-surface receptors, especially **G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs)**. When these receptors detect signals such as hormones, neurotransmitters, or other molecules, GNAQ helps relay the message inside the cell by activating pathways such as the **phospholipase C (PLC) pathway**. This can lead to changes in calcium levels and activation of protein kinase C, both of which affect cell behavior.

Mutations in **GNAQ** are significant in several diseases, particularly certain cancers. One of the best-known associations is with **uveal melanoma**, a cancer that develops in the eye. Activating mutations in GNAQ can cause continuous signaling, promoting uncontrolled cell growth. GNAQ mutations are also found in some benign vascular conditions, such as **Sturge-Weber syndrome** and **port-wine stains**, where abnormal blood vessel development occurs.

Because of its role in cell signaling and disease, GNAQ is an important focus of biomedical research. Scientists are studying how GNAQ mutations alter signaling pathways and how these pathways might be targeted with new therapies. Although directly targeting GNAQ has been challenging, drugs aimed at downstream signaling components may offer potential treatment strategies.

In summary, **GNAQ** is a key signaling gene involved in normal cellular communication, development, and disease. Its mutations are especially important in uveal melanoma and vascular disorders, making it a valuable subject in genetics, cancer biology, and targeted therapy research.

# Additional Specification Support Language

## Definitions

As used herein, “**puromycin analog**” refers to a compound structurally or functionally related to puromycin that retains at least one biological activity of puromycin, including but not limited to aminoacyl-tRNA mimicry, ribosome binding, inhibition of peptide chain elongation, induction of premature chain termination, inhibition of protein synthesis, or cytotoxic or cytostatic activity. Puromycin analogs include derivatives, salts, esters, amides, prodrugs, stereoisomers, metabolites, conjugates, and pharmaceutically acceptable forms thereof.

As used herein, “**activating GNAQ mutation**” includes a mutation that increases, prolongs, or dysregulates signaling by Gαq or a downstream pathway thereof. Non-limiting examples include mutations encoding **R183Q**, **Q209L**, **Q209P**, **R183G**, **R183L**, and functionally equivalent substitutions.

As used herein, “**vascular malformation**” refers to an abnormal vascular lesion or vascular anomaly comprising blood vessels, lymphatic vessels, capillaries, veins, arteries, or combinations thereof. Examples include capillary malformations, venous malformations, lymphatic malformations, arteriovenous malformations, mixed vascular malformations, port-wine birthmarks, and Sturge-Weber syndrome-associated vascular lesions.

As used herein, “**effective amount**” refers to an amount sufficient to produce a desired biological or therapeutic effect, including inhibition of GNAQ-mutant cells or improvement in one or more signs or symptoms of a vascular malformation.

---

## Mechanistic Language

Without wishing to be bound by theory, cells harboring activating **GNAQ** mutations, including **R183Q** and **Q209L**, may exhibit altered translational requirements, stress responses, metabolic dependencies, proliferative signaling, or angiogenic phenotypes that render such cells susceptible to inhibition by puromycin or puromycin analogs. Contacting such cells with puromycin or a puromycin analog may reduce protein synthesis, induce translational stress, impair survival signaling, decrease angiogenic behavior, or otherwise reduce the pathological contribution of the GNAQ-mutant cells to a vascular malformation.

---

## Treatment Outcome Language

In some embodiments, administration of puromycin or a puromycin analog results in one or more of: reduced number of GNAQ-mutant endothelial cells; reduced vascular lumen dilation; reduced lesion thickness; reduced erythema; reduced lesion area; reduced bleeding; reduced pain; reduced swelling; reduced abnormal perfusion; reduced inflammatory infiltration; reduced ulceration; reduced need for laser therapy, surgery, or sclerotherapy; or improved cosmetic or functional outcome.

---

## Formulation Language

Puromycin or a puromycin analog may be formulated with one or more pharmaceutically acceptable carriers, excipients, stabilizers, preservatives, penetration enhancers, viscosity modifiers, buffers, salts, surfactants, emulsifiers, polymers, biodegradable matrices, or targeting agents. In certain embodiments, the formulation is configured to provide local delivery to lesional tissue while minimizing systemic exposure.

Suitable formulations include, without limitation, topical creams, gels, ointments, sprays, foams, patches, microneedle arrays, injectable solutions, hydrogels, biodegradable depots, nanoparticles, microparticles, liposomes, polymeric carriers, antibody-drug conjugates, peptide conjugates, and implantable delivery systems.

---

## Dosing Language

In some embodiments, puromycin or a puromycin analog is administered in an amount sufficient to inhibit GNAQ-mutant cells while maintaining acceptable tolerability. The dosing regimen may include a single administration or repeated administrations. Local dosing may be preferred in certain embodiments to achieve therapeutic concentrations in the vascular malformation while reducing systemic exposure. The dose, frequency, and route of administration may be selected based on lesion size, lesion location, mutation burden, subject age, severity of symptoms, formulation type, and response to treatment.

---

## Experimental Support Paragraphs

In some embodiments, efficacy may be assessed by contacting cultured endothelial cells expressing **GNAQ R183Q** or **GNAQ Q209L** with puromycin or a puromycin analog and measuring cell viability, proliferation, apoptosis, protein synthesis, ERK phosphorylation, YAP/TAZ activity, angiogenic tube formation, migration, or expression of vascular markers. In other embodiments, efficacy may be assessed in organoid, explant, xenograft, mosaic animal, or vascular malformation models comprising GNAQ-mutant cells.

In certain embodiments, selectivity may be determined by comparing the effect of puromycin or a puromycin analog on GNAQ-mutant cells relative to otherwise comparable cells lacking the GNAQ mutation.

---

# Alternative Broad Independent Claims

62. **A method of reducing the burden of GNAQ-mutant cells in a vascular lesion, comprising locally administering puromycin or a puromycin analog to the vascular lesion, wherein the GNAQ-mutant cells comprise a GNAQ R183Q or GNAQ Q209L mutation.**

Below is exemplary broad patent-disclosure style language. It is drafted to cover puromycin and structurally/functionally related analogs for selectively reducing survival of cells harboring GNAQ mutations and for treating vascular malformation-related diseases and disorders.

## Exemplary Patent Disclosure Language

### Title

**Compositions and Methods for Targeting GNAQ-Mutant Cells and Treating Vascular Malformations Using Puromycin and Analogs Thereof**

### Technical Field

The present disclosure relates generally to therapeutic and research uses of puromycin, puromycin derivatives, puromycin analogs, prodrugs, salts, formulations, and functional equivalents thereof for reducing viability, proliferation, persistence, or survival of cells comprising one or more mutations in **GNAQ**. The disclosure further relates to methods of treating, preventing, slowing progression of, reducing symptoms of, or otherwise managing vascular malformations and vascular malformation-related conditions associated with GNAQ mutations or GNAQ pathway activation.

### Background

Somatic mutations in **GNAQ**, including activating mutations affecting residues such as Q209 and R183, are implicated in various vascular anomalies and related disorders. Such mutations may drive aberrant endothelial cell signaling, abnormal vascular development, vascular lesion formation, vascular overgrowth, or related pathological vascular remodeling. There remains a need for agents capable of preferentially reducing the survival or pathological activity of GNAQ-mutant cells, including mutant endothelial cells, perivascular cells, or other lesion-associated cells, and for therapies useful in vascular malformation-related conditions.

### Summary

In certain aspects, the disclosure provides methods of reducing the survival, viability, proliferation, metabolic activity, clonogenic capacity, engraftment, persistence, or pathogenic function of a cell comprising a **GNAQ mutation**, the method comprising contacting the cell with an effective amount of **puromycin** or an analog, derivative, prodrug, metabolite, pharmaceutically acceptable salt, solvate, hydrate, stereoisomer, isotopologue, conjugate, or formulation thereof.

In some embodiments, the cell comprises a somatic activating mutation in GNAQ. In some embodiments, the GNAQ mutation comprises a mutation at or near codon **183** or **209**. In certain embodiments, the mutation comprises **GNAQ R183Q**, **GNAQ R183G**, **GNAQ R183L**, **GNAQ Q209L**, **GNAQ Q209P**, **GNAQ Q209H**, **GNAQ Q209R**, or another activating GNAQ mutation.

In some aspects, the disclosure provides methods for treating a vascular malformation-related condition in a subject in need thereof, comprising administering to the subject an effective amount of puromycin or an analog thereof, thereby reducing survival or pathological activity of GNAQ-mutant cells in the subject.

In some embodiments, the vascular malformation-related condition is selected from capillary malformation, venous malformation, lymphatic malformation, arteriovenous malformation, combined vascular malformation, port-wine birthmark or port-wine stain, Sturge-Weber syndrome, congenital hemangioma-associated malformation, ocular vascular malformation, leptomeningeal vascular malformation, cutaneous vascular malformation, mucosal vascular malformation, soft tissue vascular malformation, overgrowth syndrome associated with vascular malformation, and any condition characterized by abnormal vascular morphogenesis, vascular overgrowth, vascular leakage, vascular ectasia, vascular nodularity, vascular pain, bleeding, inflammation, thrombosis, ulceration, functional impairment, or cosmetic disfigurement associated with GNAQ-mutant cells.

### Detailed Disclosure

#### Puromycin and Analogs

As used herein, “puromycin” includes puromycin free base and any pharmaceutically acceptable salt, solvate, hydrate, polymorph, crystalline form, amorphous form, ester, amide, prodrug, conjugate, or formulation thereof.

As used herein, “puromycin analog” or “analog thereof” includes any compound structurally related to puromycin, derived from puromycin, mimicking one or more biological activities of puromycin, or capable of reducing survival of a GNAQ-mutant cell. In some embodiments, a puromycin analog comprises a modified nucleoside portion, a modified aminoacyl portion, a modified aromatic moiety, a modified amide linkage, a modified sugar, a modified base, a modified amino group, a substituted tyrosyl-like group, or any combination thereof.

In certain embodiments, the analog is selected from puromycin aminonucleoside, O-methyl puromycin derivatives, N-substituted puromycin derivatives, aminoacyl-nucleoside analogs, puromycin-like peptidyl transferase substrates, translation-terminating nucleoside analogs, cell-permeable puromycin derivatives, masked puromycin prodrugs, antibody-drug conjugates comprising puromycin or a puromycin analog, polymer-conjugated puromycin compounds, nanoparticle-encapsulated puromycin compounds, liposomal puromycin compounds, locally deliverable puromycin formulations, sustained-release puromycin formulations, and lesion-targeted puromycin formulations.

In some embodiments, the compound binds to, mimics, inhibits, modulates, or exploits ribosomal translation machinery. In other embodiments, the compound reduces GNAQ-mutant cell survival independently of, or in addition to, effects on protein translation.

#### GNAQ-Mutant Cells

In certain embodiments, the disclosed methods are used to reduce survival of a cell comprising a mutation in GNAQ. The cell may be an endothelial cell, vascular endothelial cell, lymphatic endothelial cell, capillary endothelial cell, venous endothelial cell, arterial endothelial cell, endothelial progenitor cell, pericyte, smooth muscle cell, stromal cell, fibroblast, immune cell, melanocytic cell, neural crest-derived cell, ocular cell, leptomeningeal cell, or any cell present in, derived from, or associated with a vascular malformation.

In some embodiments, the cell is obtained from or present in a vascular lesion. In some embodiments, the cell is a human cell. In some embodiments, the cell is an in vitro cultured cell, organoid cell, ex vivo tissue cell, xenograft cell, genetically engineered cell, or cell in a subject.

In certain embodiments, contacting the cell with puromycin or an analog thereof causes one or more of decreased viability, decreased proliferation, increased apoptosis, increased necrosis, increased senescence, reduced protein synthesis, reduced clonogenic survival, reduced migration, reduced tubule formation, reduced angiogenic capacity, reduced lesion growth, reduced abnormal vascular signaling, reduced MAPK pathway activity, reduced ERK phosphorylation, reduced YAP/TAZ activity, reduced PLCβ signaling, reduced PKC signaling, reduced calcium signaling, reduced inflammatory signaling, or reduced secretion of angiogenic or lymphangiogenic factors.

#### Selectivity

In some embodiments, puromycin or an analog thereof preferentially reduces survival of a GNAQ-mutant cell relative to a corresponding wild-type GNAQ cell. In certain embodiments, the corresponding wild-type cell is of the same cell type or tissue origin. In some embodiments, the preferential reduction is at least about 1.2-fold, 1.5-fold, 2-fold, 3-fold, 5-fold, 10-fold, 20-fold, 50-fold, or greater compared with a wild-type GNAQ cell under comparable conditions.

In some embodiments, the GNAQ-mutant cell exhibits increased sensitivity to puromycin or an analog thereof relative to a non-mutant cell. In some embodiments, the increased sensitivity is measured by reduced IC50, EC50, GI50, LC50, colony formation, lesion cell burden, or viability.

In one aspect, provided herein is a method of treating a vascular malformation-related condition in a subject, comprising administering to the subject an effective amount of puromycin or an analog thereof.

In certain embodiments, the subject has, is suspected of having, or is at risk of having a vascular malformation comprising cells with one or more GNAQ mutations. In some embodiments, the method further comprises detecting a GNAQ mutation in a biological sample obtained from the subject. The biological sample may comprise lesion tissue, blood, plasma, serum, circulating endothelial cells, circulating cell-free DNA, biopsy material, skin tissue, mucosal tissue, ocular tissue, cerebrospinal fluid, or any other sample.

In some embodiments, treatment results in reduced lesion size, reduced vascular density, reduced vascular leakage, reduced lesion thickness, reduced discoloration, reduced pain, reduced swelling, reduced bleeding, reduced ulceration, reduced thrombosis, reduced inflammation, reduced neurologic symptoms, reduced seizure frequency, improved ocular pressure, improved vision, improved mobility, improved cosmetic appearance, improved quality of life, or reduced need for surgical, laser, embolization, or interventional treatment.

- malformation-associated pain, bleeding, thrombosis, ulceration, edema, inflammation, or disfigurement.

In some embodiments, the condition is a vascular anomaly classified under an International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies classification and associated with a mutation in GNAQ.

#### Administration and Formulations

Puromycin or an analog thereof may be administered by any suitable route, including topical, intralesional, intradermal, subcutaneous, intravenous, intraarterial, intraocular, periocular, intracranial, intrathecal, oral, buccal, transdermal, mucosal, inhalational, local, regional, or systemic administration.

In some embodiments, the compound is administered locally to a vascular malformation. In certain embodiments, the compound is administered topically, intralesionally, or by a local sustained-release device to reduce systemic exposure.

In some embodiments, the composition comprises a pharmaceutically acceptable carrier, excipient, diluent, stabilizer, preservative, buffer, penetration enhancer, hydrogel, ointment, cream, lotion, patch, microneedle formulation, depot formulation, injectable formulation, nanoparticle, liposome, polymeric particle, implant, microsphere, conjugate, or controlled-release matrix.

In some embodiments, the puromycin or analog thereof is formulated for selective delivery to vascular endothelial cells, lesion-associated endothelial cells, GNAQ-mutant cells, or vascular malformation tissue. Targeting moieties may include antibodies, antibody fragments, peptides, aptamers, ligands, receptor-binding agents, integrin-binding agents, endothelial-targeting agents, vascular homing peptides, or molecules that bind markers enriched in vascular malformations.

#### Dosage

An effective amount may be any amount sufficient to reduce survival or pathogenic activity of GNAQ-mutant cells or to improve one or more symptoms of a vascular malformation-related condition. In some embodiments, the effective amount is lower than an amount causing unacceptable toxicity in the subject.

In certain embodiments, the compound is administered at a dose ranging from about 0.001 mg/kg to about 100 mg/kg, about 0.01 mg/kg to about 50 mg/kg, about 0.01 mg/kg to about 10 mg/kg, or about 0.1 mg/kg to about 5 mg/kg. For local administration, the concentration may range from about 0.001 μM to about 10 mM, about 0.01 μM to about 1 mM, about 0.1 μM to about 500 μM, or about 1 μM to about 100 μM.

In some embodiments, dosing occurs once, repeatedly, continuously, intermittently, daily, weekly, monthly, or according to a schedule determined by lesion response or tolerability.

#### Combination Therapies

In some embodiments, puromycin or an analog thereof is administered in combination with one or more additional therapies. The additional therapy may comprise laser therapy, pulsed dye laser therapy, surgery, sclerotherapy, embolization, corticosteroids, beta blockers, sirolimus, everolimus, mTOR inhibitors, MEK inhibitors, ERK inhibitors, RAF inhibitors, PI3K inhibitors, AKT inhibitors, PKC inhibitors, YAP/TAZ pathway inhibitors, angiogenesis inhibitors, VEGF inhibitors, anti-inflammatory agents, anticoagulants, antiplatelet agents, analgesics, or other agents used to treat vascular anomalies.

In some embodiments, the combination therapy permits lower doses of puromycin or analog thereof, improves selectivity, reduces toxicity, enhances lesion regression, reduces recurrence, or improves durability of treatment.

#### Diagnostic and Patient Selection Methods

In certain embodiments, a subject is selected for treatment based on detection of a GNAQ mutation. Detection may be performed using sequencing, next-generation sequencing, allele-specific PCR, droplet digital PCR, quantitative PCR, Sanger sequencing, targeted mutation analysis, single-cell sequencing, spatial sequencing, RNA sequencing, immunohistochemistry, pathway activation assays, or any other suitable method.

In some embodiments, a method comprises:

2. detecting a GNAQ mutation or GNAQ pathway activation in the sample; and
3. administering puromycin or an analog thereof to the subject if the mutation or pathway activation is detected.

In other embodiments, the subject is treated without prior genetic confirmation where the clinical presentation is consistent with a GNAQ-associated vascular malformation.

#### Screening Methods

The disclosure also provides screening methods for identifying puromycin analogs useful for reducing survival of GNAQ-mutant cells. In certain embodiments, the method comprises contacting a GNAQ-mutant cell and a control cell with a candidate puromycin analog and identifying the candidate as useful if it reduces survival of the GNAQ-mutant cell relative to the control cell.

In some embodiments, the screening method comprises measuring viability, apoptosis, proliferation, protein synthesis, MAPK signaling, ERK phosphorylation, calcium signaling, vascular network formation, endothelial migration, or lesion-forming capacity.

#### Kits

In some embodiments, the kit further comprises a diagnostic reagent for detecting a GNAQ mutation. In some embodiments, the kit comprises a topical, injectable, intralesional, or controlled-release formulation.
